EN.s10: [[1]]Here is where your profile stands today on those five pillars. [[2]][[3]][[4]][[5]][[6]]Your strongest is {strongest}, at {strong_score} out of ten. Your biggest gap is {weakest}, at {weak_score}{followed_by}. That is normal: your technical expertise covers the hands-on side, and the pillars measure the management layer on top of it. Closing that layer is exactly what our eight-week mentoring program does, and it is what makes you credible as {a_target_role}.
EN.s07: Three things close that kind of gap. [[1]]Targeted knowledge: learning exactly what your target role requires, and applying it on real cases. [[2]]A recognized certification: a credential employers trust, that proves your competence before the interview. [[3]]And deliberate career positioning: a resume, a LinkedIn profile and a story that present you as the best candidate. [[4]]The CMRP certification, a clear structure and private mentoring bring the three together. Let us look at how that applies to your case.
EN.s08: The CMRP stands for Certified Maintenance and Reliability Professional. It is awarded by SMRP, the Society for Maintenance and Reliability Professionals. [[1]]On its website, SMRP describes the CMRP as the leading credential for certifying the knowledge, skills and abilities of maintenance, reliability and physical asset management professionals. [[2]]It is the only certification program of its kind accredited by ANSI, the American National Standards Institute, [[3]]following the globally recognized ISO standards. [[4]]Today, close to ten thousand professionals hold it worldwide, [[5]]and it covers five pillars of competence, assessed in a single exam.
EN.s09: [[1]]The CMRP covers five pillars. [[2]]One: business and management, aligning maintenance with business goals, budgets and the business case. [[3]]Two: manufacturing process reliability, keeping the whole process stable and capable. [[4]]Three: equipment reliability, making assets perform through failure analysis and preventive and predictive maintenance. [[5]]Four: organization and leadership, the people side of the work. [[6]]Five: work management, planning, scheduling and executing maintenance efficiently. Among these five pillars, two, three and five are mostly technical. Pillars one and four, business and management, and organization and leadership, are usually what separates a strong technician from an effective maintenance leader. [[7]]Once you are CMRP certified, you are recognized as competent in all five.
EN.s11: [[1]]Ascend Leadership Group is a coaching and mentoring firm for maintenance and reliability professionals, based in the Greater Toronto Area, in Canada. [[2]]We help professionals earn the credentials that open senior roles, and position them so the market sees it. [[3]]Our flagship program is an eight-week private CMRP mentoring program, and every professional who completed it passed the CMRP and significantly improved their competitiveness and their impact in the job market. [[4]]Coaching is always one on one, [[5]]which lets us calibrate every discussion to each candidate's personal goals. [[6]]The firm was founded by Christian Dimene, an expert in industrial maintenance and asset management, who holds the CMRP, CAMA, PMP and PSM credentials.
EN.s12: We work on four angles. [[1]]First, targeted learning and application: you learn what your target role requires, and apply it on real cases. [[2]]Second, certification readiness: a structured method, with exam simulators, to pass the certification exam on the first attempt. [[3]]Third, professional brand and market positioning: your resume, LinkedIn profile and story, aligned with the role you want. [[4]]And fourth, private coaching and mentoring: a mentor at your side every week, from the start to the end of the program.
EN.s13: [[1]]The program runs over eight weeks. [[2]]In weeks one to four, you learn and apply: each week combines learning, application, a mini-project and a coaching session. [[3]]In weeks five and six, you practice on our exam simulators, build your professional brand, and register for the exam. Week seven is your final review. [[4]]Week eight is exam week, followed by your market positioning session. [[5]]Plan for five to six hours a week. You choose your start date, and you can pause if life demands it.
EN.s14: Results matter more than promises. [[1]]One hundred percent of the professionals who completed the program passed their CMRP. [[2]]Harold, a professional engineer who already ran maintenance across seven sites at Siemens Energy, earned his CMRP in seven weeks, and is now Head of Maintenance and Facilities at Alstom. [[3]]Marvin had attempted the exam once without success, and had run out of time. With the program, he passed with more than fifty minutes to spare, and was promoted to Manager of Facilities along the way. [[4]]Angelico earned his CMRP and completed his career positioning with us. Within a month, he had landed seven interviews and received two job offers. [[5]]And the program is backed by a guarantee: if you do the work and do not pass, you get your money back.
EN.s15: There are three ways to get to your next role faster with us. [[1]]Self-paced, where you develop on your own through our curated approach, at your own pace. [[2]]The full guided program, our most popular option, which adds career positioning, a pass guarantee and a private mentor throughout. [[3]]And two certifications combined, for those who want to go further. [[4]]The prices for your region are on screen. A five-hundred-dollar discount on each is offered during your fifteen-minute roadmap debrief with us, and payment plans are available.
EN.s16: The most logical next step is simple. [[1]]Book your fifteen-minute roadmap debrief within seven days. We will answer your questions, confirm your path, [[2]]and unlock your five-hundred-dollar discount. [[3]]Then secure your place in the program with a two-hundred-dollar deposit, and choose your start date. [[4]]The booking link for your debrief session is in the email that came with this roadmap.
EN.s17: [[1]]Thank you for watching. A written copy of this roadmap is attached to the email, so you can come back to it anytime. [[2]]We look forward to speaking with you, [[3]]and to helping you take the next step in your career.
EN.s15_roi: Based on the wage gap we looked at earlier, the guided program pays for itself in {roi_range} in your new role.

FR.s08: Le CMRP signifie Certified Maintenance and Reliability Professional, soit professionnel certifié en maintenance et fiabilité. Il est décerné par la SMRP, la Society for Maintenance and Reliability Professionals. [[1]]Sur son site Web, la SMRP décrit le CMRP comme la principale certification attestant les connaissances, les compétences et les aptitudes des professionnels de la maintenance, de la fiabilité et de la gestion des actifs physiques. [[2]]C'est le seul programme de certification de ce type accrédité par l'ANSI, l'American National Standards Institute, [[3]]selon les normes ISO reconnues mondialement. [[4]]Aujourd'hui, près de dix mille professionnels le détiennent dans le monde, [[5]]et il couvre cinq piliers de compétence, évalués dans un seul examen.
FR.s09: [[1]]Le CMRP couvre cinq piliers. [[2]]Un. Les affaires et la gestion, qui alignent la maintenance sur les objectifs de l'entreprise, les budgets et l'analyse de rentabilité. [[3]]Deux. La fiabilité des procédés de fabrication, qui maintient l'ensemble du procédé stable et capable. [[4]]Trois. La fiabilité des équipements, qui assure la performance des actifs grâce à l'analyse des défaillances et à la maintenance préventive et prédictive. [[5]]Quatre. L'organisation et le leadership, le volet humain du travail. [[6]]Cinq. La gestion des travaux, pour planifier, ordonnancer et exécuter la maintenance avec efficacité. Parmi ces cinq piliers, le deuxième, le troisième et le cinquième sont surtout techniques. Les piliers un et quatre, les affaires et la gestion, ainsi que l'organisation et le leadership, sont habituellement ce qui distingue un bon technicien d'un leader efficace en maintenance. [[7]]Une fois certifié CMRP, vous êtes reconnu compétent dans les cinq.
FR.s11: [[1]]Ascend Leadership Group est un cabinet de coaching et de mentorat pour les professionnels de la maintenance et de la fiabilité, établi dans la région du Grand Toronto, au Canada. [[2]]Nous aidons les professionnels à obtenir les certifications qui ouvrent les postes de haut niveau, et à se positionner pour que le marché le voie. [[3]]Notre programme phare est un mentorat privé CMRP de huit semaines, et toutes les personnes qui l'ont terminé ont réussi le CMRP, et ont considérablement amélioré leur compétitivité et leur impact sur le marché de l'emploi. [[4]]Le coaching est toujours individuel, [[5]]ce qui permet de calibrer les discussions en fonction des objectifs personnels de chaque candidat. [[6]]Le cabinet a été fondé par Christian Dimene, expert en maintenance industrielle et en gestion des actifs, et titulaire des certifications CMRP, CAMA, PMP et PSM.
FR.s12: Nous travaillons sur quatre axes. [[1]]Premièrement, l'apprentissage ciblé et l'application. Vous apprenez ce que votre poste visé exige, et vous l'appliquez à des cas réels. [[2]]Deuxièmement, la préparation à la certification. Une méthode structurée, avec des simulateurs d'examen, pour réussir l'examen de certification à la première tentative. [[3]]Troisièmement, la marque professionnelle et le positionnement sur le marché. Votre CV, votre profil LinkedIn et votre récit, alignés sur le poste que vous visez. [[4]]Et quatrièmement, le coaching et le mentorat privés. Un mentor à vos côtés chaque semaine, du début à la fin du programme.
FR.s13: [[1]]Le programme se déroule sur huit semaines. [[2]]Des semaines un à quatre, vous apprenez et appliquez : chaque semaine combine l'apprentissage, des applications, un mini-projet et une séance de coaching. [[3]]Aux semaines cinq et six, vous vous exercez sur nos simulateurs d'examen, vous développez votre marque professionnelle et vous vous inscrivez à l'examen. La semaine sept est consacrée à la révision finale. [[4]]La semaine huit est celle de l'examen, suivie de votre séance de positionnement sur le marché. [[5]]Prévoyez cinq à six heures par semaine. Vous choisissez votre date de début, et vous pouvez faire une pause si votre situation l'exige.
FR.s14: Les résultats comptent plus que les promesses. [[1]]Cent pour cent des professionnels qui ont terminé le programme ont réussi leur CMRP. [[2]]Harold, un ingénieur qui dirigeait déjà la maintenance de sept sites chez Siemens Energy, a obtenu son CMRP en sept semaines, et il est aujourd'hui directeur de la maintenance et des installations chez Alstom. [[3]]Marvin avait tenté l'examen une première fois sans succès, et il avait manqué de temps. Avec le programme, il l'a réussi avec plus de cinquante minutes en réserve, et il a été promu gestionnaire des installations en cours de route. [[4]]Angelico a obtenu son CMRP et terminé son positionnement de carrière avec nous. En moins d'un mois, il avait décroché sept entrevues et reçu deux offres d'emploi. [[5]]Et le programme est appuyé par une garantie : si vous faites le travail et ne réussissez pas, vous êtes remboursé.
